name: Qwirkle

source.title: Qwirkle colour-blind friendly rules (2023), library-hosted copy

setup.text: Put all 108 tiles in the bag and choose a scorekeeper with pen and paper.
Draw six tiles from the bag to make your hand.

Check your hand for your biggest group of tiles sharing one inner shape/colour or one outer shape, with no duplicates, and say its size. The biggest plays those tiles to start. Ties go to the oldest player. Play goes clockwise.

turn.summary: Play tiles from your hand into one line, score, then draw back up to six. Or swap tiles instead.
steps: Choose one or more tiles that all share one inner shape/colour or all share one outer shape, with no duplicates.
Place them all in one line, touching at least one tile already played. They need not touch each other, so you can add at both ends of a line.
Score one point for every tile in each line you made or added to. A tile can count in two lines.
Draw tiles to get back to six.

Alternative: instead of playing, trade any tiles. Set them aside, draw replacements, then put the set-aside tiles back in the bag. You score nothing and you cannot trade more tiles than remain in the bag.

end: When the bag is empty, play on without drawing. The first player to use all their tiles scores 6 bonus points and the game ends.

scoring.text: One point per tile in each line you created or added to, counting existing tiles in that line.
A line of all six shapes or colours is a Qwirkle: 6 points for its tiles plus 6 bonus points, at least 12 in all.
The player who goes out first scores 6 bonus points.

tiebreak: If tied for first place, the winners share the win.

missed.text: A line can hold at most six tiles and never repeats a tile.
A tile placed at a crossing counts once for each line it is in.
You score for the whole line, not only the tiles you added.
Trading uses your whole turn and scores nothing.
You may place tiles at both ends of one line in the same turn, as long as they are all in one line.

unverified: The sheet is the colour-blind friendly edition, where colours are paired with inner shapes. It may differ in tile art from the standard box; the rules text was used as printed.
